title: Overview
description: Learn what POLIS is, who it is for, and what it means to deliver changes backed by evidence.
text: POLIS is a Go CLI and a software-change delivery protocol . It brings together behavioral specifications, change boundaries, tests, validation, and artifact integrity into a verifiable process. Designed for AI-assisted engineering, its mechanisms also work for human-led delivery. It is not an AI model, code generator, or cloud service: its role is to validate, package, and control the acceptance of changes . The problem it addresses A change may work on the producer's machine and still be incompatible with its destination repository. It can also be difficult to answer basic questions: which requirements does the change satisfy, which tests ran, which files were allowed to change, and what is the exact identity of the resulting tree? POLIS makes these questions auditable through contracts, development proof, project policies, and validation performed both by the producer and the consumer. Three foundations 1. Explicit scope. The Change Contract defines authorized changes, acceptance criteria, and mandatory proof. 2. Verifiable evidence. The producer creates a .polis package carrying validation information, identity, and traceability; its exact bytes can be checked independently. 3. Deliberate application. The consumer runs preflight before apply ; apply repeats validation against the current state and requires authorization. What POLIS does not promise - It does not replace human review or guarantee the absence of defects or vulnerabilities. - It does not sandbox arbitrary project commands; those commands may still interact with external systems. - A passing test is not universal proof that the software is correct. - Artifact integrity does not establish producer authenticity: that requires a detached signature and independently trusted consumer-supplied key. - apply does not implicitly push commits or publish releases. Roles and responsibilities Role Responsibility Examples --- --- --- Producer Specify, prove, implement, and package start , capture-red , build Reader Verify and inspect an artifact verify , inspect Consumer Validate against its own state and apply when authorized preflight , apply Where to begin Start with Installation ../installation/ and Quickstart ../quickstart/ . For the complete lifecycle, read Delivery workflow ../delivery-workflow/ . The V6 Specification https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/spec/POLIS-SPEC-v6.md governs machine contracts. The official usage guide https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/usage.md provides the complete operational command reference.

title: Installation
description: Install POLIS V6 using Go, or download the offline kit for your platform.
text: The recommended installation requires Go 1.23 or newer and Git . These instructions follow the official installation guide. Prerequisites Make sure both executables are available: bash go version git --version Install with Go On Linux, macOS, or Windows: bash go install github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/v6/cmd/polis@latest polis help polis doctor For a reproducible installation, replace @latest with a specific V6 module tag: bash go install github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/v6/cmd/polis@v6.11.1 This version was documented in the README consulted for this site. It is not a claim that this tag will always be the newest release; check GitHub Releases. Configure PATH Go installs binaries into GOBIN , or into GOPATH/bin if GOBIN is unset. If the terminal cannot find polis , add that directory to PATH . Linux or macOS: bash go env GOBIN go env GOPATH Windows PowerShell: powershell $goBin = go env GOBIN .Trim if -not $goBin { $goBin = Join-Path go env GOPATH .Trim 'bin' } $env:Path = "$env:Path;$goBin" polis doctor See the official platform-specific installation guide https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/installation.md to persist the PATH setting. Install from source To develop POLIS or use an explicitly checked-out revision: bash git clone https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis.git cd polis go install ./cmd/polis polis doctor Alternative: offline runtime The offline kit does not require Go to execute POLIS . Download polis-<tag -offline-<GOOS -<GOARCH .zip for your OS and architecture from GitHub Releases https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/releases/latest , extract it, then run bin/polis or bin/polis.exe . Git is still required, and project-specific validation commands may require other tools. See Offline runtime ../offline-runtime/ . Confirm the installation bash polis help polis doctor A BLOCKED diagnostic indicates that a required condition prevented operation. Fix the reported prerequisite or environment issue rather than treating it as a passed test.

title: Quickstart
description: Install, diagnose, and inspect validation for a Git repository before preparing a delivery.
text: This guide introduces the first commands and distinguishes configuration inspection from a verified delivery . A successful plan or gates run does not mean that a .polis package exists. 1. Install and diagnose bash go install github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/v6/cmd/polis@latest polis doctor doctor checks CLI prerequisites. See Installation ../installation/ if the binary is not on PATH . 2. Choose a Git repository Work in a repository whose state you can inspect. POLIS identifies the Git state and the policy that governs project validation. bash cd /path/to/your/project git status --short Do not discard local changes simply to satisfy the CLI. POLIS intentionally blocks ambiguous states rather than silently accepting them. 3. Preview policy generation without writing files For a root Go module, auto can generate a profile. Preview it without persisting files: bash polis init --repo . --profile auto --dry-run Automatic profile detection supports root Go modules. Other ecosystems require explicit commands through the custom profile. If you decide to persist the policy, run init without --dry-run and review the generated files before committing : bash polis init --repo . --profile auto 4. Inspect the validation plan bash polis plan --repo . plan is read-only. It shows enabled gates, dependencies, commands, and the effective policy's guarantees and limitations. Run configured gates locally with: bash polis gates --repo . gates validates project commands; it does not create or verify a delivery artifact. That requires a locked contract, the required proof, and build followed by verify . 5. Prepare a full delivery A complete delivery needs a behavioral Specification, Change Contract, authorized scope, and proof strategy. Their schemas and preconditions are normative and should not be improvised from an isolated command example. Continue with Delivery workflow ../delivery-workflow/ and SDD and TDD ../sdd-and-tdd/ . Commands shown here illustrate syntax , not ready-made valid contracts.

title: Core concepts
description: A glossary of the main POLIS objects, responsibilities, and result states.
text: Before building a delivery package, distinguish the core objects of the protocol. Glossary Concept Meaning --- --- Specification Defines expected behavior, requirements, and acceptance criteria. Project Policy Defines applicable project commands and quality gates. Change Contract Defines behavior, change scope, tests, proof requirements, and baseline identity. Locked baseline Git state and policy associated with a contract locked by polis start . Red-to-Green Observed proof of a relevant baseline failure followed by success after implementation. Green-to-Green Characterization that passes both before and after a behavior-preserving change. Evidence Bounded structured records of commands, proof, and validation decisions. Gate A policy-configured check with explicit prerequisites and outcomes. .polis A verifiable delivery package, distinct from the offline runtime bundle. Preflight Validation against the consumer environment without applying a change. PASS, FAIL, and BLOCKED are different PASS means an applicable check was completed successfully. FAIL indicates a validation failure actually observed. BLOCKED means prerequisites or environment prevented the intended validation from running. A test that never ran cannot count as Red proof. Integrity versus authenticity Hashes and checksums detect changes to package bytes. To associate those bytes with a trusted producer, the consumer must verify a detached signature against an independently supplied trusted public key . See Security and trust ../security/ . Who defines what? The Engineering Guide defines process. The V6 Specification defines machine-level contracts. The Go CLI implements the protocol. See Architecture ../architecture/ for details.

title: Delivery workflow
description: How producers prepare, prove, package, and deliver changes for independent consumer validation.
text: The POLIS lifecycle separates producing a delivery from consumer acceptance . Consumers must not inherit trust from the producer's machine. Step 1 — Prepare the change Review the expected behavior, authorized scope, tests, Project Policy, and Git baseline. A Change Contract is a versioned and validated document, not a free-form description. Given a valid strict draft and a clean repository, start locks the contract and relevant identities: bash polis start --repo /repo \ --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --contract /outside/draft-v5.json \ --out /outside/locked-v6.json A schema-v5 draft becomes a locked schema-v6 contract. The existing schema-v3 to schema-v4 locking flow remains supported. Step 2 — Establish development proof Strict feature and defect changes use Red-to-Green . Before modifying the implementation, check the proposed test paths and capture a genuine failure of the required behavior: bash polis check-red-scope --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --path internal/example test.go polis capture-red --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --out /outside/regression.patch capture-red requires a test-only delta and a failure matching the contract oracle. A behavior preserving change uses Green-to-Green instead; it does not invent a Red failure. Step 3 — Implement and validate Edit only authorized paths and preserve captured tests. Validate the working tree without building a delivery package: bash polis workspace validate --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --regression-patch /outside/regression.patch You may generate an optional contract-bound Implementation Plan after start . If used, pass the exact same plan bytes to subsequent commands that require them. Step 4 — Build and verify the artifact bash polis build --repo /repo \ --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --project application --change fix-validation \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --regression-patch /outside/regression.patch \ --out /outside/output polis verify /outside/output/artifact.polis polis inspect /outside/output/artifact.polis Confirm the actual output paths and filenames from command output. This example illustrates an unplanned Red-to-Green delivery, not a universal command for every change. Step 5 — Consume in a target repository bash polis preflight --repo /consumer /outside/output/artifact.polis Only after review and explicit authorization: polis apply --repo /consumer /outside/output/artifact.polis preflight does not apply changes to the consumer; apply revalidates before mutation. See Safe application ../safe-application/ and Baseline modes ../baseline-modes/ . Repository isolation In the canonical workflow, the policy, locked contract, Red proof, package, and signature remain outside the target worktree . POLIS also supports explicitly configured retention in .polis/artifacts/ . See the official operational guide https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/usage.md repository-artifact-retention .

title: SDD and TDD
description: How specifications and Red-to-Green or Green-to-Green proofs structure strict development.
text: POLIS distinguishes two complementary concerns. Specification-Driven Development SDD defines the behavioral contract before implementation. Test-Driven Development TDD supplies observed evidence of the development path. Specify first A strict Change Contract links identifiable requirements to acceptance criteria, implementation and test scopes, and proof commands. Specification identity and the effective policy are locked against the Git baseline before edits. A useful specification answers: - What behavior must be introduced or preserved? - Which files may change? - What concrete observation demonstrates the required behavior? - Which conditions should block the delivery? Red-to-Green For strict features and defects, the producer must demonstrate that the relevant test failed on the baseline and passes after the change . POLIS captures actual Red proof before production edits: bash polis check-red-scope --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --path internal/behavior test.go polis capture-red --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --out /outside/regression.patch A failure must match the prescribed command, exit code, and oracle. A missing executable is not regression proof. Captured tests remain immutable and are validated again in later steps. Green-to-Green Strictly behavior-preserving changes use a characterization that passes on the baseline and continues passing on the target. There is no reason to manufacture a Red failure. Optional Implementation Plan bash polis implementation-plan --repo /repo \ --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --out /outside/implementation-plan.json The plan is derived deterministically from the locked contract and remains subordinate to it. When explicitly packaged, it changes the delivery to format v6 , adding an authenticated plan member. Important limitation Validation establishes only the observable properties and execution conditions represented by the contract and its proof. It cannot prove an unrecorded implementation chronology or replace security review and semantic correctness checks.

title: Validation and gates
description: Execute quality policies, inspect dependencies, and distinguish local checks from delivery validation.
text: A gate is a Project Policy check. It may run tests, coverage, lint, or another configured command. Project Policy controls quality checks, while mandatory protocol integrity and safety invariants remain in force. Inspect before execution bash polis plan --repo . plan does not execute gates. It lists execution order, commands, dependencies, enabled gates, and the guarantees or limits of the effective policy. Run local validation bash polis gates --repo . To run selected checks or only those affected by Git changes: bash polis gates --repo . --gate lint --gate coverage polis gates --repo . --affected Required dependencies are added automatically. --jobs accepts 1 through 16; gates overlap only when explicitly marked parallel safe . Coverage remains exclusive. gates is not a sandbox . It runs configured commands in the actual repository, potentially creating caches or external effects according to project command behavior. Reuse and replay A run can produce a result manifest. POLIS lets you inspect it, conditionally reuse passing results, or replay the selection through fresh execution. bash polis gates --repo . --environment-id toolchain-v1 \ --out-run /outside/first.json polis gates --inspect-run /outside/first.json polis gates --repo . --environment-id toolchain-v1 \ --reuse /outside/first.json The environment identifier is operator asserted : it does not establish a hermetic environment or verify that external conditions really match. Reuse is disabled without an identifier. Previous results do not prove a modified repository state. PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, and DEFERRED Status Meaning --- --- PASS The applicable check completed successfully. FAIL An executed check found a problem. BLOCKED A prerequisite prevented intended execution. DEFERRED The producer deferred an enabled gate; the consumer still must execute it for supported formats. Strict, standard, and minimal strict is the default. standard keeps test.complete and disables generated coverage by default. minimal disables generated project-quality gates by default. None of these settings relaxes mandatory structure, integrity, scope, or application guarantees. See Project Policy ../project-policy/ for gate configuration and Artifacts and verification ../artifacts-and-verification/ for how validation becomes part of delivery.

title: Artifacts and verification
description: Understand .polis packages, V6 formats, inspection, and detached digital signatures.
text: A .polis file is the output of a validated delivery. It packages the change, contracts, and evidence required for verification and consumption within the specification's schemas and size limits. Build a delivery package The producer uses polis build only after locking a baseline and satisfying mandatory development proof. Then check the resulting artifact independently: bash polis verify /outside/output/artifact.polis polis inspect --format json /outside/output/artifact.polis verify checks package bytes, required members, checksums, schemas, and supported proof consistency. inspect exposes validated metadata without applying the change. Package formats in POLIS V6 Produced artifact Package format Key property --- --- --- Delivery without explicit plan format v5 Eight canonical members, including the embedded baseline. Delivery with an Implementation Plan format v6 Nine members; the plan is bound to the package and its evidence. POLIS V6 names the protocol and CLI generation. It does not mean every new package necessarily uses format 6. The presence of an Implementation Plan selects the package format. Supported historical formats remain readable under their compatibility rules. Checksums do not identify producers A checksum validates a relationship between bytes and digest, but does not prove who created them. Optional authenticity uses an Ed25519 detached signature verified using a consumer-supplied, independently trusted public key. bash polis sign --key private.pem \ --out artifact.polis.sig artifact.polis polis verify \ --signature artifact.polis.sig \ --trusted-key public.pem \ artifact.polis Protect the private key. Consumers must not simply trust a public key selected by the package itself. Plans and traceability With an Implementation Plan, inspect can report relationships between requirements, acceptance criteria, implementation steps, and proof. Plan presence never replaces execution of required validation. Reading is not applying verify and inspect operate on the artifact alone. To determine whether it can safely be used against a specific target repository , run consumer preflight ../safe-application/ before authorized application.

title: Safe application
description: Understand consumer preflight, apply revalidation, and explicitly authorized local commit modes.
text: Consumers must verify a delivery against their own current Git state and environment . A producer PASS or past preflight PASS is not permanent authorization to modify files. 1. Verify the package bash polis verify artifact.polis polis inspect artifact.polis Review the scope, patch contents, and configured policy commands. Such commands may have external effects. Worktree isolation is not a security sandbox for untrusted code. 2. Run preflight bash polis preflight --repo /target /outside/artifact.polis preflight verifies the package, baseline admission, isolated target, development proof, and applicable gates—including those deferred by the producer. It does not apply the patch to the consumer . If the repository changes afterwards, that earlier PASS cannot establish that application is still safe. 3. Apply only after authorization bash polis apply --repo /target /outside/artifact.polis apply repeats validation before changing files and verifies target-tree identity after application. In canonical apply-only mode, it preserves HEAD and the real Git index. Transactional checks and rollback exist for failures, but operators must investigate errors and verify reported recovery state. Commit modes The default is --commit-mode none : apply content without a commit. When the artifact contains valid commit intent, two explicit options are available: bash Requires interactive terminal and approval: polis apply --repo /target --commit-mode prompt /outside/artifact.polis Explicitly authorizes a local commit without prompting: polis apply --repo /target --commit-mode auto /outside/artifact.polis auto is explicit local authorization , not a workaround for an agent without a terminal. Neither mode automatically runs git push , signs a commit, or publishes a release. Different baselines The default --baseline-mode strict requires exact locked base commit equality. compatible admits proven clean descendants after full validation. permissive permits a broader attempt with warnings, without ignoring real conflicts. Read Baseline modes ../baseline-modes/ before relaxing the default.

title: Offline runtime
description: Distribute POLIS to agents and machines without installing Go or requiring network access.
text: POLIS V6 offers a platform-specific portable offline runtime . The ZIP contains the native executable, specification, JSON schemas, manifest, and supporting files needed by the CLI. It is distinct from a .polis code-change delivery package. Download an offline bundle Choose the ZIP matching your operating system and architecture from official releases https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/releases/latest : text polis-<tag -offline-<GOOS -<GOARCH .zip After extraction, run bin/polis on Unix-like systems or bin/polis.exe on Windows. Go is not required to run the included binary. Dependencies and limits - Git must be installed and available on PATH . - The executable must match the host operating system and CPU architecture. - Project Policy commands may still require project-specific compilers, runtimes, network access, or tooling. - The bundle does not include a target repository or its Project Policy . Export a local bundle From an installed POLIS CLI: bash polis export --out /outside/polis-v6-offline.zip Export produces a deterministic ZIP with a manifest and checksums, without reading target repository data. --executable and --runtime let release tooling include externally built target binaries without executing them on the exporting host. Using the kit with agents Give an offline agent the appropriate bundle and only the contracts and artifacts it is explicitly authorized to access. The agent still needs the project's policy and clear boundaries between read-only checks, validation, and mutation. Consult the offline runtime specification https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/spec/POLIS-OFFLINE.md before distribution.

title: Change Contract
description: How a contract defines behavior, file scope, required proof, and the locked baseline.
text: The Change Contract is the structured source of obligations for an individual delivery. It makes change limits enforceable and links requirements to acceptance criteria and proof. What a strict contract represents - Specification: a versioned description of expected behavior. - Requirements and acceptance criteria: traceable links between intent and acceptance. - Change scope: source paths authorized to change. - Test scope: allowed paths for tests captured as proof. - Proof commands: commands and oracles validating development behavior. - Baseline lock: Git state identity and effective policy digest bound to the locked contract. Draft and lock The newer workflow passes a schema-v5 draft to polis start , which produces a locked schema-v6 Change Contract . Compatibility with draft schema v3 to locked schema v4 remains available. bash polis start --repo /repo \ --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --contract /outside/draft-v5.json \ --out /outside/locked-v6.json The lock must be established on a clean Git baseline before implementation . Do not rewrite a locked contract to excuse changes that exceeded scope; establish a new legitimate baseline and lock when requirements change. Scope is executable scope.allowed paths constrains implementation changes. Captured test files must also fall within the designated test scope. Before creating Red tests: bash polis check-red-scope --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --path tests/feature test.go This accepts paths that do not yet exist , since it validates the proposal rather than file contents. The later capture checks the actual test-only delta. Optional commit intent A schema-v5 draft may include a commit message bound into the locked contract and package. It only creates a commit when the consumer explicitly invokes apply --commit-mode prompt or auto . Authoritative schema reference Contracts have precise serialization, size, validation, and migration rules. Do not treat a partial UI example as a production contract template. Refer to the V6 Specification https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/spec/POLIS-SPEC-v6.md , versioned schemas https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/tree/main/spec/schemas , and CLI for valid inputs.

title: Project Policy
description: Configure explicit checks with Project Policy schema v3 and validation levels strict, standard, and minimal.
text: Project Policy defines how POLIS validates a project: commands, gates, dependencies, environments, and enablement decisions. The effective policy digest is bound to the locked Change Contract. Begin with inspection bash polis init --repo . --profile auto --dry-run polis plan --repo . auto recognizes root Go modules. Other ecosystems use --profile custom with explicitly declared commands. Do not blindly reuse language-specific gates across projects. Validation levels Level Behavior --- --- strict Default: retains the strongest generated project gates. standard Keeps test.complete while disabling generated coverage by default. minimal Disables generated project-quality gates by default. None of these levels disables mandatory structural, integrity, scope, baseline, or application invariants. Disabled gates and their reasons remain visible. Commands use argv, not shell strings Policy commands are executed as direct arguments. POLIS rejects recognized shell-wrapper forms such as bash -lc and sh -c . For complex validation, create a version-controlled runner in the project and declare its direct executable invocation. Illustrative command object: json { "argv": "python", "scripts/validate project.py" , "cwd": ".", "timeout seconds": 600, "environment": { "mode": "clean", "pass": "PATH", "HOME" } } This is only a command object , not a complete valid Project Policy. Use the authoritative schema to write one. Inherited versus clean environments environment.mode=inherit forwards the process environment. clean starts from a controlled base and forwards explicitly named variables, plus applicable Windows bootstrap variables. Environment values are not stored in package evidence. Dependencies and concurrency Gates may declare depends on . POLIS validates their dependency graph and computes a deterministic order. Concurrent execution requires an explicit safety assertion; coverage executes exclusively. Changing policy requires a new lock A locked contract binds the policy digest. Changing the policy breaks that identity. Do not weaken gates just to manufacture a passing delivery: review the policy and create a new corresponding baseline and contract.

title: Baseline modes
description: How strict, compatible, and permissive govern package admission against different Git states.
text: A package is built from a locked Git baseline. Consumers may have the same or a different commit; POLIS requires an explicit policy for handling that difference. Strict — default bash polis preflight --repo /consumer \ --baseline-mode strict artifact.polis Requires consumer HEAD to match the artifact's locked base commit exactly . This is the most restrictive mode and the CLI default. Compatible — validated descendant bash polis preflight --repo /consumer \ --baseline-mode compatible artifact.polis Allows a different clean HEAD when descendant ancestry is proven and all required context, proof, scope, policy, and deterministic target-tree checks pass. It is not automatic conflict resolution. Permissive — ancestry may be unproven bash polis preflight --repo /consumer \ --baseline-mode permissive artifact.polis May attempt admission without descendant ancestry, while still requiring patch, scope, policy, and target-tree validation. Unproven ancestry is reported as a risk. This mode does not ignore conflicts. Embedded historical proof Newer formats include an authenticated locked-baseline snapshot so development proofs can be replayed when original Git objects are absent. The permissive mode alone can accept an explicit waiver when historical baseline proof is unavailable, with reduced guarantees reported: bash polis preflight --repo /consumer \ --baseline-mode permissive \ --allow-missing-baseline-proof artifact.polis This waiver is unavailable in other modes. Using it requires a deliberate decision about the missing assurances. Preflight and apply are separate preflight mode is not automatically carried over into apply . Repeat the intended mode explicitly in the authorized apply command, which will revalidate the current consumer state.

title: Security and trust
description: Understand untrusted packages, signatures, security boundaries, and consumer assurances.
text: POLIS is designed to fail closed on invalid inputs and incompatible states. It is nevertheless important to distinguish its actual guarantees from operator responsibilities. Trust boundaries A .polis package must be treated as untrusted input . Verification enforces member inventory, size limits, schema validation, checksums, and evidence consistency before admission. The Change Contract restricts authorized file paths and the consumer checks exact target-tree identity. Authenticity requires an external trust root Detached Ed25519 signatures can bind the package's exact bytes to a trusted producer only when the consumer supplies an independently trusted public key . A key found inside the package cannot appoint itself as an authority. bash polis verify --signature artifact.polis.sig \ --trusted-key producer-public.pem \ artifact.polis Isolation is not sandboxing build , preflight , and apply perform relevant validation in isolated repositories or worktrees. That protects Git state but does not necessarily isolate processes, networks, or credentials . Review policy commands and proof before executing untrusted content. Current state matters - preflight checks the current consumer state, not a permanent approval. - apply repeats validation before modifying files. - A nonzero exit caused by missing prerequisites does not prove a test found a defect. - A hash proves byte integrity, not semantic security of source code. Explicit authorization apply requires authorization for the intended repository. --commit-mode auto requires deliberate authorization to create a local commit. Successful validation must never be taken as permission to publish a release or push a commit. Where assurance ends Even a correctly verified patch may be unsafe in scenarios not covered by tests. Verifiable validation increases auditability , but cannot replace code review, threat modeling, or appropriate project testing.

title: Traceability and evidence
description: Connect requirements, plans, and proof without mistaking metadata for observed execution.
text: POLIS evidence describes what ran, against which identities, and with what results . It makes deliveries auditable without persisting arbitrary full command-output dumps in the package. Traceability chain A strict change connects: 1. Identifiable requirements in the Specification. 2. Acceptance criteria linked to those requirements. 3. Development proof and gates prescribed by the contract and policy. 4. An identified Git target tree and verifiable delivery package. With an optional Implementation Plan, test and implementation steps link to requirements and acceptance criteria; the plan becomes part of a format-v6 package. What evidence records Structured evidence includes command identity, exit code, duration, SHA-256 digests, byte counts, truncation flags, and declared environment metadata. It does not persist complete raw stdout/stderr streams as proof. This limits size and potentially sensitive output exposure, but means full execution logs cannot necessarily be reconstructed from the package alone. Historical records are not current validation polis gates run manifests and workspace checkpoints help resume work, but an old report cannot substitute for validation of changed source. Input and declared environment identities must be re-evaluated. Inspect traceability bash polis inspect --format json artifact.polis polis status --repo /repo --package /outside/artifact.polis Available fields depend on artifact format and supplied inputs. See the V6 Specification https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/spec/POLIS-SPEC-v6.md for normative record semantics.

title: CLI commands
description: A practical POLIS V6 command reference organized by workflow stage.
text: This page is a purpose-oriented index. For complete options, run polis help <command , polis <command --help , or consult the official command reference https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/usage.md command-reference . Discovery and preparation Command Purpose --- --- help Show read-only syntax and operational guidance. doctor Check CLI prerequisites and environment. init Generate Project Policy using a chosen profile. plan Preview effective policy, gates, dependencies, and assurances without execution. status Summarize workflow state and the next step using supplied inputs. bash polis help polis help start polis doctor --format json polis init --repo . --dry-run polis plan --repo . Validation and planning Command Purpose --- --- gates Execute Project Policy gates, including selected or affected subsets. workspace validate Validate a locked change without producing a .polis package. workspace status Compare source identity against an unauthenticated checkpoint. implementation-plan Generate an optional plan derived from the locked contract. bash polis gates --repo . --affected polis implementation-plan --repo /repo \ --contract /outside/locked-v6.json \ --out /outside/implementation-plan.json Delivery production Command Purpose --- --- start Lock the contract to a baseline and effective policy. check-red-scope Check that proposed test paths are authorized. capture-red Capture genuine Red proof for a Red-to-Green change. build Validate and produce a verifiable change package. bash polis start --repo /repo --policy /outside/policy-v3.json \ --contract /outside/draft-v5.json \ --out /outside/locked-v6.json Reading and consumption Command Purpose --- --- verify Validate package integrity and consistency. inspect Read validated package metadata. preflight Validate against the consumer without applying changes. apply Revalidate and apply, only after authorization. sign Produce a detached package signature. export Create an offline runtime bundle, not a delivery package. bash polis verify artifact.polis polis inspect --format json artifact.polis polis preflight --repo /consumer artifact.polis Choose the appropriate operation - Use plan to preview validation and gates to execute local checks. - Use workspace validate to validate without a package and build to create one. - Use verify for package bytes and preflight for a particular target repository. - Use authorized apply only when intending to modify consumer files. Options and semantics may evolve within the V6 release line. Always check polis help from the installed CLI for exact behavior.

title: Exit codes
description: Interpret CLI exit statuses and distinguish validation failure from an execution blocker.
text: POLIS uses stable exit categories for automation, without conflating different failure modes into a generic result. Exit status categories Code Category Operational meaning --- --- --- 0 PASS The operation completed under its contract. 2 Usage error Invalid syntax, flags, or arguments. 3 Invalid artifact/signature Package or cryptographic verification rejected. 4 Blocked environment or authorization Preconditions prevented execution or authorized commit. 5 Baseline mismatch Consumer state does not satisfy the selected baseline mode. 6 Validation failure Proof, gate, contract, or other validated condition failed. 7 Apply failure Error during apply, commit, or rollback. Diagnose beyond the code Exit status is only the most compact signal. Read the contextual diagnostic and, where appropriate, structured output: bash polis doctor --format json polis plan --repo . --format json polis preflight --repo /consumer --format json artifact.polis Do not assume all commands use every exit code for the same underlying issue. The CLI help gives command-specific outcomes. Test failures versus environment failures When a required compiler or executable is missing, the intended test did not run . In Red-to-Green workflows, that does not demonstrate the baseline fails for the specified behavioral reason. In CI, treat BLOCKED as an unaccepted delivery until the prerequisite is restored—not a success with a warning.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Diagnose installation errors, gates, scope, baseline issues, and rejected application.
text: POLIS blockers typically indicate that an identity, precondition, or proof needs attention. The right response depends on the reported cause , not solely the exit code. polis: command not found After go install , check go env GOBIN and go env GOPATH . Add the binary directory to PATH and run polis doctor . See Installation ../installation/ . Gate BLOCKED due to missing tooling Read the gate diagnostic and check required dependencies in the intended environment. BLOCKED is not a failing test assertion. Do not rewrite a Red oracle to accept missing tooling as proof of an actual regression. start rejects the baseline Inspect the worktree, real index, policy identity, and contract schema. start is designed to happen before production edits. Do not reset, stash, or delete someone else's work to make it pass. check-red-scope rejects a path The proposed path must fit both the authorized test scope and overall Change Contract scope. Review test scope.allowed paths and scope.allowed paths before editing files or revising the contract. Gate reuse was denied --reuse requires matching input identities and an explicit --environment-id . That identifier is an operator assertion, not proof the actual environment matches. For fresh evidence, rerun the gates rather than forcing invalid reuse. Preflight rejects the baseline The default strict mode requires exact base commit equality. Investigate Git history and only consider compatible or permissive when their risks are understood and every required check still passes. See Baseline modes ../baseline-modes/ . Apply fails Stop further mutations. Inspect the CLI diagnostic, git status , the index, and target tree. Transactional recovery attempts to restore state, but the operator must verify the reported result before retrying. Find authoritative help bash polis help polis help preflight polis help apply Consult the full official usage guide https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/usage.md , and open an issue https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/issues for reproducible discrepancies.

title: Architecture
description: How the engineering guide, normative specification, and Go CLI work together.
text: POLIS separates engineering process , verifiable contracts , and executable implementation . This prevents narrative guidance from silently redefining the meaning of package bytes. Repository layers Layer Directory Responsibility --- --- --- Engineering Guide guide/ Process, scope, evidence obligations, and delivery practices. POLIS Specification spec/ Normative schemas, package rules, hashing, evidence, signing, and application. CLI cmd/polis/ Command-line interface and operations. Implementation internal/ Supporting Go code for execution and validation. Documentation docs/ Operational guides, installation, examples, and design decisions. Normative authority If an Engineering Guide explanation conflicts with a package rule, the versioned Specification governs machine-level semantics. The CLI is the reference implementation, but its actual behavior still needs to be verified through tests and execution. Producer and consumer The producer executes development proof and produces a target Git tree and .polis package. The consumer receives untrusted bytes, validates integrity and applicable rules, and performs its own checks before any mutation. This separation limits claims such as “it passed on the author's machine”: consumer identity, source state, and effective commands also matter. Dependencies and distribution The CLI is written in Go and uses Git for change identity and application. The V6 module path is github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/v6 . In addition to Go installation, the project distributes platform-specific offline kits containing the binary and supporting CLI resources. Maintaining this website Source documents are maintained in content/ Portuguese and content/en/ English . The static generator build.py creates HTML, language-matched navigation, and separate search indexes. Presentation lives in assets/styles.css and assets/nautical.css ; interactions live in assets/app.js . Website explanations can evolve independently of CLI implementation.

title: Contributing and evolution
description: Find POLIS authoritative sources and report documentation or implementation issues.
text: POLIS source code and history are maintained on GitHub. Before proposing changes, review the current specification and behavior of the CLI revision in question. Repository and key documents - POLIS source code https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis - README and project entry point https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/README.md - V6 Specification https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/spec/POLIS-SPEC-v6.md - Operational guide https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/docs/usage.md - Changelog https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md - Issues and bug reports https://github.com/MarcosAlves90/polis/issues Proposing a fix Report the observed behavior, source revision/version, reproduction steps, expected and actual results, and supporting evidence. For protocol semantic changes, establish the applicable specification first. Contributing to this website The site is designed for small, independently maintainable changes: 1. Create or edit a Portuguese Markdown file in content/ and its English counterpart in content/en/ , with matching filenames and title , description , group , order , and source frontmatter. 2. Write sections in Markdown and reference the relevant official source. Use English-language route names when linking from translated content. 3. Run python build.py to generate static pages and language-specific indexes in dist/ . 4. Run tests and review routes, search, responsive behavior, and alignment with the POLIS repository. This site is an educational and operational guide; it does not establish a competing normative specification.
